page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most CPU-bound workloads. The instance achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 1578.98 and a multi-core score of 16657.34. In Geekbench testing, it recorded a single-core score of 1253.0 and a multi-core score of 7455.0, with software compilation scoring 14249.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 921.81 GB/sec for cached small blocks, but uncached large-block read and write speeds drop to 72.44 GB/sec and 50.62 GB/sec respectively. Notably, the PassMark memory score of 1797.16 is categorized in the bottom 25%, indicating a potential performance bottleneck for memory-intensive operations relative to its processing capabilities.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is structured for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. It demonstrates average efficiency in static web serving at 9.51 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 15.83 million operations per second. For machine learning, it handles small 135M LLM text generation at 169.31 tokens per second, but performance drops to a weak 22.42 tokens per second for 7B model prompt processing. The ecs.c4.4xlarge is best suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations.
